title: Childhood poverty, shoes, boudin and stealing milk
summary: He recalls shining shoes, secondhand shoes, trading eggs for boudin in the country, stealing milk, and a shortcake lunch for school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Is that why you stopped quoting your aunt?

When that time the show was a nickel. The show was a nickel. I used to shine the shoes. Sell the newspapers at the same time. I sold the newspapers to shine the shoes. I'd go out there on Sunday and say they'd make a dollar and a half, two dollars. My mama would give me fifteen cents out of my money. Out of my money. Didn't know what a new pair of shoes was. Every pair of shoes I wore was second hand.
Who got them first?
So my other had them before I got them. I'd go to the shoemaker and get me a pair. How much you want for them shoes? Twenty-five cents? Thirty cents? Get a good pair of shoes fifty cents. You know?
Oh, you bought you went and bought shoes from shoemaker. Shoemaker. No new shoes.
Never they went on new shoes until I got to be a man. That's right. Didn't know what overcoat was.
What'd you do in cold weather?

Staying inside. Staying inside. It was cold during that time. Then when I was a boy coming up my mama called herself to send me out in the country to live, Tibidale. Chicken eats a little egg. I used to be there and catch it when they get hot and soon he dropped it I had it. Oh. Boudin man passed by. Boudin, Boudin, Boudin, Boudin, Boudin. I said, yeah, he said, what you got? I said, I got two eggs. Take them two eggs and give me a big old hunk of Boudin.
What's Boudin?
That's blood size.
Oh. You swapped the eggs for that?
Swapped the eggs for that Boudin.

Me and that boudin at night, ate that boudin and... Drink some water. Huh? Drink me some water. No, go out there and steal me a quarter of milk. Where did you steal milk? Steal me a quarter of milk. And cream, bread, cream, bread, cream, bread, milk and boudin.
Where did you steal the milk?
Up the people's steps.
Oh.

I got out running a spidery with me. I knew I could run. Anytime I reached up and got my big apple off my head, I was gone. You couldn't catch me with a hound dog. Turn them callers doing 90 miles? No, turn them callers. Fell down with a bottle of milk in my hand one night. Pooleys got behind me one night. Fell down, broke the bottle. I stood there and had half of my hand. Went up there and started having the milk bottle. Quarter of milk.
I was just chasing you. I had a hard time. I was coming up.

See, I was raised with a step-four. My father died when I was five years old. My step-four used to cut my hair. Sometime he didn't cut it. Sometime my mama cut my hair. And sent me to school. I didn't go to school like real children did. Write on sleeve. Pencil. Chalked right with the chalk. And during that time people used to make shortcakes. I'd have shortcake. No bread, shortcake. Shortcake and Magnolia milk. Shortcake peanut butter. Shortcake blackberry jam. Going to school. And when you go to school, people do that at that time, you can ask for lining up. They give you a mammy cookie or a genius graham cracker, animal cake, something like that. I used to love to go to school.
Well you ate the shortcake for breakfast or you took it to school for lunch? I took that for my, that was my lunch. Better not eat it all. Better not eat it all.
Oh, you just ate part of it for breakfast and you saved the other? Yeah.
